solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mark well beaten on bum

indicators.note: bum as slang adjective means bad or faulty, so these letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about a well-placed smack on someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like the noun being struck; it is the slang adjective for 'bad', telling you to rearrange BEATEN ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is the note-writer's instruction to observe carefully, literally 'note well'.

clue.text: Goose bumps covering either side of tight butt

indicators.note: the shuffled goose letters wrap around the letter taken from tight
to bump things is to knock them about, so the letters of the word goose are jolted into a new order
tight begins and ends with the same letter, so taking either of its sides gives that one letter

explanation.surface: A goose-pimpled image of someone clenched up at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either side of tight' gives T, which is the same whichever end you choose; the scrambled GOOSE letters go around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name someone who is the target of jokes, the comic's put-upon sidekick.

clue.text: Unclothed scanty dons recognised in colour

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the seen letters wear the stripped word inside them

parts.note: recognised means seen, noticed

indicators.note: stripping a word of its clothes removes its outer letters, its first and last

parts.note: scanty means meagre, thin or sparse

explanation.surface: Skimpily dressed figures caught out in a bright hue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unclothed' strips the outer letters from the synonym for scanty; 'dons' means the word for recognised wears that remainder inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bluish-green shade named after the sea, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Gambling without ace, so folding

indicators.note: without means the following letter is left out of the word

parts.note: playing, as at cards or a casino, is gambling
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A poker player loses an ace and so folds the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folding' sounds like giving up a hand at cards, but it is the sense of layering: a ply is a fold or layer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply cloth or yarn is to fold or twist it in layers, the root of two-ply and plywood.

clue.text: Put charge on account, such as a solicitor might do

definitions.text: such as a solicitor might do

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece put on another follows it

parts.note: a charge is a cost or price

explanation.surface: Billing a client on account, as a lawyer might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it is one who solicits on the street, a prostitute approaching clients.
explanation.definitionFit: A street solicitor approaches and propositions passers-by, which is exactly to waylay and address them boldly.

clue.text: Half-impeded one stopping to trick crews in contests

indicators.note: something stopping a word plugs it, sitting inside it

parts.note: to trick someone is to con them

indicators.note: only the first half of the synonym for impeded is used

parts.note: impeded means hampered, held back
I is the Roman numeral one
to ship is to man or take on board as crew

explanation.surface: Someone half-hindered gets in the way of a trick to win races for rowing crews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' applies to a synonym of impeded, not to the printed word; 'stopping' means that half plus one plugs the word for trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournaments decided to find the title holder are competitions, or contests.

clue.text: Concerning power tax

parts.note: over can mean concerning or about, as in a row over money
in electrical terms the load is the power drawn by a circuit

explanation.surface: A complaint about an energy levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax' looks like a noun levy, but it is the verb: to strain or burden.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax something is to strain it beyond comfortable limits, to burden it too heavily.

clue.text: Part-time occasional judge died

parts.note: odd means occasional, as in the odd visit
OB is short for obiit, Latin for died, seen on gravestones

explanation.surface: A part-time occasional judge has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual, piecemeal work done now and then is temporary and not a full-time post.

clue.text: Bristol University hates to chase old man over skills assessments

indicators.note: to chase is to follow behind, so these pieces come after the turned father
in a down answer, over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
Bristols is British rhyming slang (Bristol City = titty) for breasts, so a Bristol is a tit
hates means detests

explanation.surface: A university in Bristol loathes pursuing an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bristol' looks like the city's university; it is rhyming slang, Bristol City for a breast, giving TIT.
explanation.definitionFit: These are exams measuring a person's natural abilities, so they assess skills.

clue.text: A core of iron coated in corrosive type of resin

indicators.note: coated in means the pieces sit inside the word for corrosive

parts.note: an acid is a corrosive substance

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letters, the outer ones removed

explanation.surface: Talk of an iron rod protected by corrosive coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core of iron' gives RO, its middle two letters; A and RO are 'coated in' ACID.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a gum resin from Australian grass trees, a specific kind of resin.

clue.text: Hardy at last depicting frailty, regularly and extremely tenderly

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of depicting
regularly takes every other letter of frailty
extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of tenderly

explanation.surface: Thomas Hardy finally portraying human weakness gently and often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' suggests the novelist, but it is the adjective: tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough, resolute and showing courage under hardship; a hardy person has grit.

clue.text: Old coins, forged English copies, purser finally removed from cargo

indicators.note: forged means faked, so the letters of English plus copies are recast
removed from means a letter is taken out of the word for cargo

parts.note: cargo is freight

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of purser

explanation.surface: Fake coins and copies on a ship, with the purser's share taken from the cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges E and COPIES into PIECESO; 'finally' gives R from purser, 'removed from' FREIGHT to leave FEIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: These were Spanish silver dollars worth eight reales, the classic pirate treasure, so old coins.

clue.text: Controversial Eastern European recording device

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland, an Eastern European
mic is short for microphone, a recording device

explanation.surface: A contentious microphone made in Eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemical argument is a strongly contentious attack, so the adjective means controversial.

clue.text: Feeble, leaderless idiots — they stifle progress

indicators.note: leaderless removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: limp means feeble, weak
asses are fools, idiots

explanation.surface: Weak, rudderless fools who block every advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadlocks are situations where no way forward can be found, so they halt progress.

clue.text: Upper-class criticised, first to last, group with reduced means of support?

definitions.text: group with reduced means of support?

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter moves to the end of the word

parts.note: sniped means made sniping, critical remarks

explanation.surface: Posh critics rearranging a group whose funding has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced means of support' sounds financial; it means a single leg, as these beings have one foot.
explanation.definitionFit: One-footed creatures are a group with fewer legs to stand on, reduced physical support.

clue.text: Excluding congress from scheme, briefly producing tension

indicators.note: briefly cuts the word short by its last letter

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
tonic as an adjective describes muscle tension, producing tone

explanation.surface: A political plan that leaves Congress out, building tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'congress' looks like the American legislature; it is sexual intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A purely affectionate relationship is one without sexual intercourse, so it excludes congress.

clue.text: Beginner was aware of live broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: was aware of means knew and live means be, which together are said like the answer

explanation.surface: A novice knew about the live transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer to an activity, especially online, is a novice or beginner.

clue.text: Fight setter with tirade about church, one connected with meltdown?

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: about means the word for tirade goes around the church abbreviation

parts.note: a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A setter rows and rants about the church in a nuclear crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meltdown' suggests a reactor accident; here it is literal melting down of old metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in waste metal sells it on to be melted down and reused.

clue.text: Responds to actress — briefly moving

indicators.note: moving means the letters are moved into a new order
briefly cuts the last letter off the word actress

explanation.surface: Someone reacts to an actress's short, emotional performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final S of ACTRESS; 'moving' rearranges ACTRES.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer or behave in reply to something is to respond to it.

clue.text: Rector's second gun "discovered" in box

indicators.note: in places the gun's middle letter inside the box

parts.note: a crate is a box

indicators.note: discovered, in quotes, means dis-covered: the word gun loses its outer cover letters

explanation.surface: A rector's assistant finds a firearm in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes on 'discovered' ask for the literal sense, with its cover off, leaving U of gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest serves under the rector, his second in command.

clue.text: Centrally paralysing criminal's money overseas

indicators.note: criminal's stands for criminal is, crooked, so the letters are bent out of order
centrally takes the central letters of paralysing, dropping two from each end

explanation.surface: A crook's cash, siphoned off in a paralysing scam abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centrally' gives RALYSI, the middle six letters; 'criminal's' then shuffles them.
explanation.definitionFit: These are currency units of Saudi Arabia, Qatar and others, money used abroad.

clue.text: Dogs run into dimwit son I pulled back

indicators.note: into puts the run abbreviation inside the word for dimwit

parts.note: a bozo is a dimwit
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: pulled back means the son abbreviation and I are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Dogs run at a foolish son who is pulled away.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Russian wolfhounds, a breed of tall hunting dogs.

clue.text: Somehow sweatier, so to speak

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A wry remark that someone has got sweatier, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms flagging that words are used loosely or figuratively.

clue.text: Only partially suppressed the first craving

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is suppressed: two of its letters are hushed up and the rest kept

explanation.surface: An urge that was only half stifled the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing E and F from THE FIRST leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong desire for something, not only drink, is a figurative thirst.
